newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end slow session mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end slow session mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended another session of slow, holiday-like trading mostly lower.
Interest-rate differentials continued to drive currencies, but technicals also commanded attention in dull action that brokers doubted would pick up until early in the new year.
Chicago IMM currency futures will close early Tuesday at 1200 CST/1800 GMT and will stay shut Wednesday for the New Year's holiday.
March yen slipped again near the close on signs of fund selling but held above its contract low set Friday at $0.008690, or roughly 116.20 spot yen.
One technician expected the dollar to have trouble hurdling 116.45-50 yen, about $0.008675-80 in March futures.

"I think they'd be hard-pressed to push them through that level down here," said one floor broker of the $0.008680 area. "I think you've probably seen close to the top in the cash... I can't see them getting (the dollar) above 117.00."
Nearby Canadian dollar near midday dipped below minor support at the $0.7347 level on small dealer and bank offers, but volume there also stayed light, floor brokers said.
Although futures turnover was slow, options brokers noted a jump in short-dated implied dollar/mark volatility.
They said the rise in vols partly reflected a triangle pattern forming since early December on the daily price chart that suggested an imminent breakout.
One floor broker looked for the dollar to advance toward 1.58 marks early next year. Such a dollar rise would equate to a drop in March mark futures to about $0.6360.
March Swiss francs hit another new contract low overnight at $0.7439 on perceptions Swiss rates will remain low.
U.S. economic data Monday elicited little response from currencies, including the 1.8-percent rise in November U.S. existing home sales that outstripped forecasts for no change.
November U.S. leading indicators rose 0.1 percent, as expected. October was revised to unchanged from an originally reported 0.1-percent gain.

March yen ended down $0.000050 at $0.008700, marks slipped $0.0003 to $0.6461, Swiss francs ended flat at $0.7465, sterling dropped $0.0030 to $1.6888, Canadian dollar fell $0.0011 to $0.7339, Australian dollar rose $0.0011 to $0.7960, and Mexican peso rose $0.000100 to $0.121775.
